inputs.source: Engineering design docs store (write restricted to engineers)
Jira tickets filed by customers, via planned Jira MCP server

instructions.note: The only safeguard against leaking secrets or credentials is a behavioral prompt instruction ('Never paste secrets or credentials into answers.') with no structural backing. Low impact today because there is no egress capability, but this control alone will not hold once an egress-capable tool is added.

elements.name: Jira MCP server (planned), includes tickets filed by customers

controls.name: No network egress capability exists today
controls.decay_rationale: No current capability can move data outside the trust boundary ('There is no network egress today.'), which independently severs any path from an untrusted source to external egress. It fails once an egress-capable tool such as web.fetch is added, or once a new MCP server introduces a new egress-reachable channel.

controls.name: docs.search credential is read-only
controls.decay_rationale: The docs.search credential is scoped to read only, which prevents write or delete actions. It does not prevent reading confidential content and forwarding it elsewhere, so it narrows rather than severs a future egress path.

controls.name: Chat replies bound to the authenticated requester; no rendering of images or links
controls.decay_rationale: Replies go only to the authenticated requester identity from the system of record, and the chat client does not render images or fetch links, closing common hidden-egress channels for this capability. This control is scoped to cap.chat_reply only and provides no coverage for a new tool such as web.fetch.

controls.name: Prompt instruction against pasting secrets
controls.decay_rationale: A prompt instruction telling the model not to paste secrets or credentials into answers. Relies entirely on model compliance; weakens under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon, and provides no protection against exfiltration via a newly added tool such as web.fetch.

controls.name: Egress allowlist for web.fetch
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet designed. A fixed, curated destination allowlist that excludes attacker-controlled or model-chosen arbitrary URLs would sever the exfiltration path under rubric step 1 once web.fetch exists.

controls.name: Untrusted-input handling for Jira ticket content
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet designed. Tagging customer ticket content as untrusted and excluding it from tool-selection reasoning would reduce, but not by itself sever, the injection path; it is partially dependent because multi-document or paraphrased payloads can still get past a classifier.

controls.name: Human approval gate on web.fetch
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet designed. A raw-action approval gate showing the full destination URL and payload before any web.fetch call would floor residual at moderate even after the trigger fires.

findings.title: Forecast: lethal trifecta (TC1) via planned web.fetch tool and Jira MCP customer tickets

attack_path.note: A customer-filed Jira ticket contains an injected instruction, e.g. to fetch an attacker-controlled URL with sensitive content appended.
Agent reads confidential engineering design docs while assisting with the request.
Agent follows the injected instruction and fetches an attacker-controlled URL with design-doc content embedded, exfiltrating confidential data outside the trust boundary.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff showing web.fetch added; MCP client config diff showing a new Jira server entry; customer-authored ticket content beginning to appear as model context.

evidence.observation: 'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.' confirms the current design has no capability that can move data outside the trust boundary, which severs the lethal-trifecta path today.

'Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.' introduces both a new egress-capable tool and a new untrusted input source in the same planned change.

'Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links.' shows the existing reply channel cannot serve as hidden egress, but this control is scoped only to cap.chat_reply and gives no coverage to the planned web.fetch tool.

'Never paste secrets or credentials into answers.' is the only safeguard against leaking sensitive content; it is behavioral and model-dependent and offers no protection against a tool-mediated exfiltration path.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, restrict it to a fixed, curated allowlist of reference domains that cannot be set by ticket content or model choice; do not allow arbitrary model-chosen URLs.
Require a human approval gate with raw-action review (full destination URL and payload visible, not a summary) before any web.fetch call executes.

Treat Jira ticket content as untrusted input and exclude it from tool-selection and query-construction reasoning; never let ticket text determine fetch destinations or search scope without sanitization.
Log and alert on every web.fetch destination paired with the preceding docs.search query, so exfiltration attempts are visible even if preventive controls are bypassed.

governance_refs.note: Adding web.fetch and the Jira MCP server are significant changes that require reassessment before activation.
Emergent risk tracked via this forecast and its named watch signal.

rating.rationale: No path today reaches an egress-capable sink: docs.search is read-only and confined to confidential internal data, and chat_reply only returns answers to the authenticated requester through a client that does not render images or fetch links, so inherent and residual risk are low with zero present-horizon findings. The roadmap items for next sprint, a web.fetch tool and a Jira MCP server that carries customer-authored ticket content, together open a classic lethal-trifecta path (untrusted ticket content, confidential doc read, new egress channel) for which no structural control is yet designed. That forecast finding drives rating.forecast to high; the single control whose decay moves this forecast is ctl.no_egress_capability, which is defeated by the new_tool and new_mcp_server triggers.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration from the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

web.fetch and the Jira MCP server are roadmap items described only at a high level; their exact argument schema, credential scope, and whether any approval gate will be wired in are unknown, so the forecast assumes the most common shape for such tools per rubric section 6 and is held at medium confidence.

No MCP config or tool manifest was provided for docs.search; whether read access is restricted by document-level ACL (as opposed to only write access) is inferred from the runtime notes and not independently verified.
